response.sql:
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope
),
stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) AS mean_avg FROM pair_avg
),
kept AS (
  SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_feerate, p.avg_feerate - s.mean_avg AS excess
  FROM pair_avg p
  CROSS JOIN stats s
  WHERE p.avg_feerate > s.mean_avg
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT k.orderslink, k.acctscope, k.avg_feerate, k.excess,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY k.acctscope ORDER BY k.excess DESC, k.orderslink ASC) AS rnk
  FROM kept k
)
SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, rnk
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY acctscope, rnk;

assumptions.assumption: The inner joins drop fees with no matching order or user, as the request specifies. Users are matched on userstamp, which the schema does not declare UNIQUE; if it has duplicates, the join will inflate the averages.
AVG ignores NULL feerate values, so a pair whose feerates are all NULL gets a NULL average and is excluded by the strict comparison. The mean of pair averages also ignores NULL averages.
A NULL users.acctscope is treated as its own scope group, so those pairs can be kept and ranked. If NULL scopes should be excluded, add AND u.acctscope IS NOT NULL to the join.
Averages and excess values are returned unrounded, as the request specifies, and the output is ordered by scope and then rank.
